title: Association between overuse of short-acting β2-agonists and the risk of major adverse cardiovascular events among patients with asthma
authors: Lai CC, Chen CH, Wang YH, Wang CY, Wang HC
population: Patients with asthma in the Taiwan asthma pay-for-performance database, 2011 to 2019
funder: not read: the full text requires a subscription and is absent from PubMed Central. The Europe PMC grant list for the article names Cardinal Tien Hospital grants and 'AstraZeneca Taiwan' grant ESR-18-13978.
result: 28,500 patients with overuse (3 or more canisters a year) and 203,470 with 0 to 2 canisters. After inverse probability of treatment weighting, 1-year major adverse cardiovascular events were 2.82 against 0.99 per 100 person-years (adjusted HR 1.25, 95% CI 1.12 to 1.39); non-fatal myocardial infarction HR 1.28 (1.09 to 1.50), ischaemic stroke 1.26 (1.08 to 1.46) and mortality 1.40 (1.24 to 1.58); haemorrhagic stroke was not significantly increased. The dose-response was non-linear, with risk peaking at 6 to 8 canisters a year.
